meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction, no sub-state fiscal distinction)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended, consolidated by Law of 25 March 2020); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), restricted following ECJ Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20 (22 November 2022); CSSF Regulation 12-02 on AML/CFT obligations (as amended); EU Regulation (EU) 2015/847 on information accompanying transfers of funds; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (as amended); Law of 2 September 2011 on access to professions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization of the certifying resolution plus sworn translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory layered CDD: screen all UBOs, directors, managers and signatories against OFAC SDN, UN Consolidated Lists, EU consolidated restrictive measures and domestic Luxembourg freezing lists; verify PEP status (family and close associates included, FATF Recommendation 12) via commercial database; document source of funds and source of wealth for the constitution capital; evidence sanctions search results with timestamp; report any anomaly to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier, CRF) under Article 5 of the Law of 12 November 2004 and suspend the transaction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBRC) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), https://www.lbrc.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must use the Latin alphabet and may be registered in Luxembourgish, French, German or English; the RCS requires phonetic distinctiveness from existing registrations, not merely visual distinction; misleading or confusing transliterations are rejected.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Luxembourg / Grand-Duché (requires prior ministerial authorization and demonstrated corporate link)
Chambre de Commerce / Chambre des Métiers
construction / développement immobilier (requires licensed promoter status)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The non-confusion certificate issued by the RCS is valid for 60 days; the incorporation deed must be executed within that window or a fresh application is required. If the RCS rejects a name, the applicant may: (1) re-file with a modified name directly; (2) file an administrative complaint with LBRC within 15 days of refusal; (3) challenge a maintained refusal before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) within 3 months; (4) for refusals based on ministerial approval of sensitive tokens, appeal to the Tribunal administratif within 3 months of the ministerial decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted. A Luxembourg SARL must maintain a registered office in Luxembourg under the Law of 10 August 1915 and the Law of 31 May 1999 on domiciliation. An approved domiciliation company may provide the registered seat only for administrative purposes; a pure virtual office with no physical industrial or storage presence is not permissible for the compression-molding manufacturing activity and would fail commercial substance, social security and product liability requirements. Physical operating premises in Luxembourg are mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-High: approximately 55-65% probability of an unannounced inspection by the Inspectorate of Labour and Mines (ITM) and social security centre (CCSS) within the first 12 months of registered employees; approximately 25-35% probability of an unannounced visit by the tax administration (ACD) within the first two operating years; risk increases materially if only domiciliation substance is detected.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, in particular Articles 710-1 to 710-23 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée/S.à r.l.); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies, as amended.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Demande d'inscription au Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés together with the signed and dated articles of association (statuts) and capital payment certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The registered capital of a Luxembourg S.à r.l. must be at least EUR 12,000 and must be fully subscribed at incorporation. At least 25% of each cash share must be paid up before registration; the balance remains callable under the articles. The paid-in portion must be evidenced by a Luxembourg bank certificate. No separate statutory escrow account is mandatory, but if the articles require immediate payment beyond 25%, the notary or bank must hold such amounts in a blocked account until the RCS registration extract is obtained.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: (1) The founders, having subscribed for the entire 12,000 EUR share capital of [Company Name] S.à r.l., hereby approve the share subscription and allotment as set out in Annex 1. (2) The registered office is adopted at [street address], L-[postal code] Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, and the managers are authorized to execute the lease and registration formalities. (3) [Manager Name] is appointed manager of the S.à r.l. with sole or joint signature authority. (4) The manager is authorized to open bank accounts, sign tax and social declarations, and file the constitutive documents with the Luxembourg Business Registers. Adopted unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name verification and corporate statement preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) and appointed legal counsel/notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name availability request with LBR or obtain an RCS extract confirming no prior identical registered corporate name. Instruct counsel to prepare the French-language articles of association (statuts) and the statutory corporate object for ISIC 3240 production of silicone tactile sensory fidgets.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of shareholders and managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, resubmit a corrected name variation or appeal by letter to LBR. A refusal on name grounds does not affect the rest of the formation file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the articles of association by all shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the statuts in Luxembourg law terms, including share capital split, registered office, corporate object, management powers, and fiscal year. All shareholders must sign the instrument; notarization is recommended to allow direct filing by the notary and smooth bank account opening.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Omissions or typographical errors are corrected by a notarial erratum or a rectification deed before submission to RCS; resubmission does not restart the statutory incorporation timeline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Luxembourg bank account and deposit of minimum capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a bank account in the name of the future S.à r.l. or in trust for the future company. Deposit at least EUR 3,000, representing 25% of the minimum EUR 12,000 capital, and obtain the bank certificate of capital payment for the notary and RCS application.
required_dossiers: Passport or ID of shareholders and managers
AML/KYC declaration and source of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional KYC information, provide an ownership chart, notarized copies of passports, and financial source documents. If the bank refuses, another Luxembourg bank may be used without altering the RCS filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic RCS filing application, attaching the executed statuts, bank capital certificate, declaration of compliance signed by the manager, and proof of registered office. Upon acceptance, obtain the RCS extract and Luxembourg corporate number (matricule national).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RCS issues an irregularity notice, file the requested correction or supplementary declaration within the deadline stated in the notice. A refusal may be appealed before the competent district court; a corrected refiling is normally accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers; Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, the mandatory legal notices are published by LBR. Within one month, file the beneficial ownership declaration in the RBE, identifying every shareholder with more than 25% control and the natural-person manager.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: RBE omissions are corrected by an updated beneficial ownership declaration filed with LBR. Delayed publication may be resolved by obtaining an official RCS extract confirming the pending registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration tax, social, and administrative clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes; Administration de l'enregistrement; Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS); Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM); municipal authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, obtain the Luxembourg VAT number through the direct tax administration, register with CCSS for social security purposes if hiring employees, complete municipal registration of the business premises, and, if applicable, obtain the general establishment authorization under the Law of 2 September 2011.
required_dossiers: Lease or ownership deed for business premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the establishment authorization is refused or queried, submit a revised application with corrected fire safety or premises data. Tax registration or VAT issues are cured by filing a written clarification and, if necessary, obtaining an informal advance ruling.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie (Directorate for Industry) and municipal authorities for the general establishment authorization; Administration de l'environnement for environmental matters.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable for ISIC 3240 compression molding of food-grade silicone tactile sensory fidgets because this activity is low-risk and does not require a sector-specific industrial license. If the production premises fall within the commercial/industrial scope of the Law of 2 September 2011, a standard establishment authorization (autorisation d'établissement) must be obtained.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency) under the Minister for the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no full environmental impact assessment report is required for a small silicone compression-molding unit. If installed capacity or pollution potential exceeds Annex II thresholds of the Luxembourg EIA Law of 15 May 2018, a screening decision (catégorie 4 or simplified evaluation) may be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Process and sanitary wastewater must comply with applicable communal sewer regulations and EU environmental quality standards under Directive 2000/60/EC. Volatile organic compound and solvent emissions, if any, are subject to the Industrial Emissions Directive 2010/75/EU thresholds. Silicone scrap, packaging waste, and any waste oils must be segregated, stored, and removed by authorized waste collectors under the Luxembourg Law on Waste of 21 March 2017.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: CGDIS (Corps grand-ducal et d'incendie et de secours) fire safety certification for the production area; structural load inspection certificate for the building floors by a certified engineer; ITM (Inspection du travail et des mines) workplace clearance covering machine safety, CE conformity of equipment, occupational health, and employee working conditions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; common filing portal: guichet.lu (MyGuichet).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate a Luxembourg SARL in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) to obtain a 16-digit business identification number and a Luxembourg TIN. Step 2: Register with the ACD for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax. Step 3: Register for VAT with the AEDT using the national single registration form, providing constitutional documents, RCS extract, proof of registered office, and identity of authorised signatories. Step 4: Receive a Luxembourg VAT number (LU + 8 digits) from the AEDT used for domestic supplies and intra-Community transactions. Non-resident foreign entities carrying on taxable supplies in Luxembourg must register directly through the AEDT's simplified non-established VAT registration procedure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Luxembourg SARL is an opaque, fully taxable resident company subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax; no pass-through is available; worldwide income is taxable with treaty and unilateral relief for foreign source income; no tax-exempt zone applies to a standard SARL.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No 'check-the-box' election exists under Luxembourg law. A SARL may elect to join a Luxembourg fiscal unity (group taxation) with resident subsidiaries under Article 164bis LIR. Under Article 175bis LIR, a joint venture company may opt for transparency if owned at least 95% by two resident parent companies from different EU member states or treaty partners, subject to conditions. Anti-hybrid elections are not discretionary; EU ATAD rules override inconsistent treatments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 30,000 annual turnover exemption threshold ('franchise') for established small businesses; non-resident suppliers have no de minimis threshold for VAT registration in Luxembourg when making taxable supplies in Luxembourg. Intra-Community distance sales to Luxembourg consumers exceed EUR 10,000 per calendar year triggers Luxembourg VAT registration; B2B supplies may trigger registration if the customer is required to self-assess under reverse charge mechanisms.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg mandates B2G electronic invoicing through a PEPPOL-compliant platform for public procurement; no general B2B real-time fiscal clearance, API stamping, or digital invoice stamping applies. VAT returns and recapitulative statements must be filed electronically via MyGuichet; invoices must be issued within the statutory timeframe, retained for ten years, and contain all VAT invoice requirements under Articles 5 to 9 of the Luxembourg VAT law.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% VAT) applies to supplies of goods dispatched or transported by the seller or purchaser outside the European Union, and to intra-Community supplies to a purchaser holding a valid EU VAT identification number, provided the goods physically leave the territory and evidence is kept in the prescribed export file. Services supplied to businesses outside the EU are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT under the B2B place-of-supply rule; certain ancillary services are zero-rated as exports of services where the recipient is established outside the EU.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic export summary declaration lodged via Luxembourg Customs / Single Administrative Document or e-Export system)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR consignment note (showing dispatch from Luxembourg and arrival in third country)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer confirmation evidencing payment by the foreign buyer
Commercial invoice matching the customs declaration and transport evidence
Purchase order or contract proving ownership transfer and export sale
Proof of the purchaser's VAT identification number and status for intra-Community zero-rated supplies
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rated export claims are audited on the basis of complete, coherent and consistent documentary evidence; missing or inconsistent proof results in VAT reassessment at the standard rate, late payment interest, and administrative fines up to the amount of the tax evaded. Fraudulent or abusive zero-rating claims are treated as tax fraud under Article 68 of the Luxembourg VAT law, triggering penalties of up to ten times the evaded tax and criminal fines plus imprisonment. The AEDT may claw back unjustified zero-rating for up to five years after the chargeable event and ten years in cases of fraud, with succession of penalties and publication of assessments.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the Eurosystem framework alongside the European Central Bank (ECB). The BCL, established by the Law of 23 December 1998, is the competent monetary, payment-systems and balance-of-payments statistical authority. Anti-money-laundering and prudential conduct supervision of credit institutions and payment/electronic-money institutions is vested in the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) under the Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended, and CSSF Circular 18/698. Significant Luxembourg banks are subject to joint prudential supervision by the ECB through the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains full and unrestricted convertibility on both current account and capital account. Formal exchange controls were abolished by the Law of 23 December 1988, and Luxembourg is bound by the free movement of capital under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. The euro is fully convertible; there is no prior-authorisation regime, no foreign-investment screening, and no BCL licensing gate for remittances. Profit and dividend repatriation is subject only to corporate-law formalities: distribution requires an ordinary shareholders' resolution and the SARL's net assets must not fall below subscribed capital plus non-distributable reserves (Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, Article 710-1 for SARLs, as amended). No tax-clearance certificate is required for dividend remittance, although a 15% Luxembourg withholding tax applies unless reduced by an applicable double-tax treaty (e.g., EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no obligation to repatriate export proceeds into euro. An exporter may freely hold, hedge, or deploy foreign-currency receipts. However, the SARL must maintain its statutory books and prepare annual accounts in EUR under Luxembourg GAAP (Lux GAAP); realised and unrealised FX differences are recognised in profit or loss. Luxembourg banks report anonymised balance-of-payments statistics (BPM6 classification) to the BCL for Eurosystem purposes, which is a statistical reporting obligation of the bank, not a regulatory approval or conversion mandate.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Compte Courant) + Capital Escrow Account (Compte Séquestre)
Operational Account / Trade Finance Account (LC, Guarantees)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Epargne de l'Etat (BCEE – Spuerkeess)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account + Operational Trade Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM – supplementary treasury rail only. A CSSF-licensed or EU-passported electronic money institution (EMI) operating in Luxembourg under PSD2 may onboard the SARL quickly and is operationally capable of pooling Platform Pay (Amazon marketplace) payouts, providing multi-currency IBANs and making SEPA/MT103 domestic and cross-border payments. Legal constraints: an EMI may not extend credit, may not issue commercial letters of credit or bank guarantees, and is not a prudentially acceptable venue for equity-capital escrow or significant trade disbursements. Third-country (non-EU) offshore EMIs without an EU passport or a Luxembourg branch are legally barred from opening accounts for a Luxembourg corporate. The SARL must therefore anchor its treasury in a fully licensed credit institution and may use an EMI only as a secondary collections/wallet conduit.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance is effectively mandatory where any director, signatory, or ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) is a non-EEA resident. Under CSSF-guided AML/CFT practice, Luxembourg banks require face-to-face identification or, in limited cases, video identification supplemented by apostilled corporate documents and notarised powers of attorney. Fully remote opening is permitted only if all directors and UBOs hold eIDAS-qualified EU/EEA digital identities and the bank accepts qualified electronic signatures. Since the SARL has non-resident ownership flexibility, the directors should budget for at least one physical onboarding interview in Luxembourg; alternatively, a duly mandated Luxembourg-licensed professional (lawyer, notary, or chartered accountant) may complete the bank's KYC protocols on behalf of the entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity – non-EU ultimate beneficial owner without a clear tax residence or corporate chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies of all natural-person UBOs; official tax-residence certificates; Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) excerpt; full organisational chart to final individuals; independent adverse-media screening report; bank reference letter from the UBO's home institution; sworn source-of-wealth statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial share-capital injection funded by an interposed trust or third-country intermediary without a documented funding trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised deed of subscription; bank statements of the ultimate funder; source-of-wealth file (dividend resolutions, sale proceeds, employment records); executed gift or loan agreements where the funds do not originate from the UBO's own business; corporate registry certificate of the transferring entity; explanation of the economic rationale for the intermediate structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly formed SARL lacking operating history or demonstrable economic substance in Luxembourg
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan aligned to ISIC 3240 (silicone tactile fidget manufacture); EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC and REACH compliance certificates for food-grade silicone; signed lease for registered office and warehouse space in Luxembourg; projected local payroll and employment schedule; supplier purchase agreements; marketplace seller agreements (Amazon) evidencing the commercial model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border supplier payments to third countries (e.g., silicone polymer and mould imports from Asia) suggesting possible trade-based money laundering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed commercial contracts with dated invoices; Incoterms terms on each purchase order; EU customs import declarations (ICS/SAD); third-party pre-shipment inspection certificates; product-liability insurance; transfer-pricing local file with an arm's-length benchmarking study; end-use statement confirming consumer fidget toys, outside any dual-use export-control scope.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: the SARL's minimum share capital of EUR 12,394.68 is deposited before incorporation into a blocked Capital Escrow Account (compte séquestre) opened by the founders at the chosen Luxembourg bank; the bank releases the funds to the Operational Account upon registration in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS). Subsequent injections arrive as SWIFT MT103 wires denominated in EUR from the shareholder's home bank to the SARL's LU-format IBAN. The Remittance Information (field 70) must state: 'Share capital contribution – SARL [legal name] – deed dated [date]' so that the bank classifies the flow for BCL/ECB balance-of-payments statistics as direct-investment equity capital (BPM6 instrument E1). Before crediting, the bank verifies the funder's identity and source of funds, and requires the notarised contribution deed and updated RBE excerpt. No BCL foreign-exchange approval is required; credits are typically effected within one to three business days.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Three-tier clearing design: (i) SWIFT MT103 for open-account payments to suppliers of silicone polymer, injection/compression moulds, pigments, and packaging – each wire is referenced to the underlying purchase order and invoice with Incoterms discipline and archived in the SARL's AML file; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600) issued by the Luxembourg bank in favour of overseas suppliers for large raw-material consignments – typically 100% at-sight or deferred 60–120 days, payable against compliant shipping documents (bill of lading, packing list, inspection certificate); (iii) Platform Pay (Amazon Marketplace) receipts settle as biweekly SWIFT MT103/SEPA batches into the EUR operational IBAN; the SARL may either accept Amazon's proprietary Currency Converter (which embeds an FX margin) or request payout in USD and execute a matching EUR forward with the Luxembourg bank, which is materially cheaper for sustained Platform Pay volumes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF) – tenors up to 24 months under ISDA/CSA documentation; available from Luxembourg credit institutions without BCL authorisation; EMIR clearing and reporting obligations limited to the non-financial counterparty (NFC-) hedging exemption.
FX Swaps / Cross-Currency Swaps (EUR/USD, EUR/CNH) – principal and interest exchange structures aligned to trade-receivables financing and working-capital funding.
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) (EUR/CNH, EUR/INR, EUR/TRY) – permitted hedging vehicles for payables in onshore-inconvertible currencies, settled in EUR or USD on a net basis.
Plain Vanilla FX Options (EUR call / USD put and inverse pairs) – premium-protected budget-rate certainty for large Platform Pay receipts and material capex purchase contracts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined corporate income tax (CIT) and net wealth tax (IF) annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD), Luxembourg Inland Revenue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 December of the year following the financial year (e.g., FY ending 31 Dec 2024 due by 31 Dec 2025); electronic filing extension may be granted by ACD
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest at 0.8% per month or part thereof; late-filing penalty up to 10% of CIT liability; administrative fines up to EUR 3,000; forced tax collection and director liability for persistent non-payment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (comptes annuels) deposit with the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the financial year-end (shareholders' approval within 6 months; RCS filing within 1 month after approval); e.g., by 31 July following a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered astreinte (periodic penalty) for continued default; personal liability of managers for damages; judicial dissolution and strike-off from the RCS for serious or repeated non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership (RBE) annual confirmation and change declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation on the anniversary of the initial RBE declaration; any shareholding or beneficial-ownership change filed within one month of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 125,000 and possible criminal penalties for willful non-compliance; directors may be held jointly liable; administrative strike-off is not triggered by this item alone

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for a SARL if, for two consecutive financial years, it exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds: balance-sheet total EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average workforce of 50 employees. An audit may also be required by a shareholder request or by the articles of incorporation; regulated financial institutions and insurance undertakings are always subject to statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002 and Luxembourg Companies Law) for statutory annual accounts; IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted for individual accounts and mandatory for consolidated accounts of listed companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must maintain an internal UBO register and file initial beneficial-ownership data with the RBE. The registered data must be confirmed annually on the anniversary of the initial filing. Any share transfer that changes beneficial ownership requires an updated RBE declaration within one month and contemporaneous updating of the register of members; share transfers for SARL are not filed as separate annual RCS returns.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 – 2,200 per annum for professional registered office and domiciliation agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – 17,000 per annum for a statutory audit of a small-to-medium Luxembourg SARL
